ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From 2x-y-2≥0, obtain the boundary y=2x-2, and the region is below it; from x+2y-1≥0, obtain the boundary y=(1-x)/2, and the region is above it; from 3x+y-8≤0, obtain the boundary y=8-3x, and the region is below it. Therefore the feasible region is the triangle enclosed by these three straight lines. Find intersections pairwise: y=2x-2 and y=(1-x)/2 intersect at (1,0); y=2x-2 and y=8-3x intersect at (2,2); y=(1-x)/2 and y=8-3x intersect at (3,-1). So the vertices of the triangle are (1,0), (2,2), and (3,-1). The x-coordinates within this triangle are all positive, and the slope of the line OM is k=y/x. On a line segment, a point is a convex combination of the endpoints, and x>0, so the value of y/x lies between the slopes of the endpoints; therefore only the vertices need to be checked. The slopes corresponding to the three vertices are respectively 0/1=0, 2/2=1, and -1/3=-1/3. Hence the minimum value is -1/3.
